title: Free one-vertex completions of a nonfree product chain
statement: Use the finite totally ordered sets $[r]=\{0<\cdots<r\}$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $m\geq0$ and $n\geq1$ be integers and let $P=\{0,\ldots,m\}\times\{0,\ldots,n\}$ have the coordinatewise order. A strict chain means a finite nonempty sequence of distinct elements of $P$ increasing in this order. Call a chain free if both coordinate projections are surjective and it contains $(b,0)$ and $(b,1)$ for some $b\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$. Let $\tau$ be a strict chain whose first coordinates contain every element of $\{0,\ldots,m\}$, whose second coordinates contain $1,\ldots,n$, and which contains no pair $(b,0),(b,1)$. Let $(p,1)$ be its first vertex with second coordinate $1$. The initial segment of $\tau$ ending at that vertex is exactly $(0,0)<\cdots<(p-1,0)<(p,1)$, interpreted as just $(0,1)$ when $p=0$. The free strict chains obtained from $\tau$ by inserting exactly one vertex are precisely the chain obtained by inserting $(p,0)$ immediately before $(p,1)$ and, when $p>0$, the chain obtained by inserting $(p-1,1)$ immediately after $(p-1,0)$. The former has its unique vertical $0$-to-$1$ pair in positions $p,p+1$, and the latter in positions $p-1,p$, with positions numbered from zero.
